args.name: Sela Thorn

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at pier four, grey braid, salt-stained coat
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; never looks anyone in the eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line; keeps mending her net.
properties.wants: Will row the party to the old chapel for two silver, but never at night; expects them at pier four at first light.
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm.

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.
I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

args.why: New NPC the GM voiced; name is spelled Sela and Sella at the table.

properties.played_as: Huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks; generous and teasing with the party.
properties.wants: Looks after the party; served stew on the house.
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her.

args.name: The Tarred Gull

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks; fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

args.why: New place where the party rests.

args.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: According to Sela, Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago on the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Sela's account links the mine flood to the bell; second-hand from her grandmother.

args.name: The Kelp Mother

properties.statement: Local belief says the Kelp Mother pulls children down by the ankles if they stand too close to the water; the GM left it unconfirmed.

sources.quote: The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

args.why: Rumor from fishermen; the GM did not confirm it is real.

args.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: According to Bram, Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.
She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

args.why: Where the table last saw Sela.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

args.why: The fact is about Saltmere Mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, about an hour's walk from Gullwick. Entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted, a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of church and old candle wax. Thirty paces in, the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: Closed and flooded; bad air inside (Oren took damage).

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

args.why: The party visited and saw the mine.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water only the bell tower and two broken arches stick out, hung with seaweed. At midnight, pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water, like a congregation, and vanish when the bell stops.
properties.state: The bell rang twelve times at midnight; the humming is much louder than two nights ago.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows.

args.why: The party saw the chapel and the shapes.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

args.why: The GM advanced the hidden clock from 2 to 3 after the louder bell.

properties.what_changed: Teo fished a wet hymn-book page out of the flooded Saltmere Mine with "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin; Teo says it is Mira's handwriting, so she was there.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

args.why: New physical lead on Mira; the handwriting identification is Teo's claim.

properties.next_step: Tomorrow at first light Sela rows the party out and they dive to the drowned chapel at low tide; Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight. Not at night.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

args.why: The party's agreed plan for the thread.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings a bell that sank with the old chapel? Unconfirmed player guess: Dana and Priya suspect harbor-master Maren Vosk is in the cult running the choir; nothing at the table supports it yet.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that.

args.why: Record the players' suspicion as a guess on the thread, not as a fact about Maren.
